labels.value: This import has already been undone, or is being undone now. Refresh the list to see where it has got to.

labels.shortDescription: Import undo: refused before a commit
labels.value: Only an import that has run can be undone. Import the rows, or leave it: a preview changes nothing.

labels.shortDescription: Import undo: refused after the deadline; {0} is the deadline
labels.value: The time to undo this import ended on {0}. The records it created are ordinary records now; delete any you do not want by hand.

labels.value: Kept: something recorded after the import points at this record, such as an activity or a relationship.

labels.shortDescription: Import undo journal: kept, records are credited to this household

labels.shortDescription: Import undo journal: kept, a person is still here

labels.shortDescription: Import undo journal: kept, no access to delete
labels.value: Kept: you do not have access to delete this record, so the undo left it in place.

labels.value: ID field people are matched on

labels.value: Match a row to an organization you already have by

labels.value: Matches an organization with exactly the same name, ignoring capitals and extra spaces. Two organizations that share a name, such as two branches, are taken as one.

labels.shortDescription: Import wizard: what the organization ID rule does and risks
labels.value: Matches on an ID your other system gave the organization. Only as good as the IDs: a value typed into the wrong record matches the wrong organization.

labels.shortDescription: Import wizard: the ID field organizations are matched on

labels.shortDescription: Import wizard: several matches option, most recently changed

labels.value: The row is rejected with the reason and nothing is written for it. The safe choice: a row loaded into the wrong duplicate is hard to notice.

labels.shortDescription: Import wizard: what using the most recent of several does and risks
labels.value: The row is loaded into whichever record was changed last. Use it only when you know your duplicates and the newest is the one you keep.
